claim: The International System of Units (SI) defines seven base units anchored to fundamental physical constants, providing a universal measurement standard

evidence.title: SI Base Units (BIPM)
evidence.finding: The 2019 SI redefinition anchors all seven base units to exact values of fundamental constants: speed of light (metre), Planck constant (kilogram), caesium frequency (second), elementary charge (ampere), Boltzmann constant (kelvin), Avogadro constant (mole), luminous efficacy (candela)

evidence.title: The CODATA 2017 values of h, e, k, and NA for the revision of the SI (Metrologia)
evidence.finding: The fundamental constants used to define SI units are known to extraordinary precision, enabling reproducible measurements worldwide

scoreReasoning.correspondence: SI units are directly realized in national metrology labs worldwide; the second is defined to 16 significant figures
scoreReasoning.coherence: All seven base units form a coherent system; derived units follow consistently from dimensional analysis
scoreReasoning.convergence: Adopted by virtually every country; the 2019 redefinition achieved global consensus at the General Conference on Weights and Measures
scoreReasoning.pragmatism: All international trade, science, engineering, and medicine use SI units or calibrate against them

claim: Every physical measurement has quantifiable uncertainty — the GUM framework provides systematic methods for evaluating and expressing measurement uncertainty

evidence.title: Guide to the Expression of Uncertainty in Measurement (BIPM GUM)
evidence.finding: The GUM, adopted by all major metrology bodies, provides a unified framework for evaluating Type A (statistical) and Type B (systematic) uncertainty components

evidence.title: An Introduction to the GUM (Metrologia)
evidence.finding: Measurement uncertainty is not error — it quantifies the dispersion of values attributable to the measurand, enabling rigorous comparison of results across laboratories

scoreReasoning.correspondence: Uncertainty budgets are directly verified by interlaboratory comparisons; NIST and PTB routinely achieve part-per-billion agreement
scoreReasoning.coherence: The GUM framework is mathematically rigorous, based on probability theory and propagation of distributions
scoreReasoning.convergence: International consensus through JCGM; adopted by ISO, NIST, PTB, NPL, and all national metrology institutes
scoreReasoning.pragmatism: Without uncertainty quantification, no measurement result is scientifically meaningful; required for all calibration certificates

claim: Scientific measurements are reproducible — independent laboratories using calibrated instruments and standardized methods obtain consistent results within stated uncertainties

evidence.title: 1,500 scientists lift the lid on reproducibility (Nature 2016)
evidence.finding: While a 'reproducibility crisis' exists in some fields, fundamental physics measurements (constants, particle masses, atomic spectra) reproduce to extraordinary precision across decades and continents

evidence.title: CIPM Mutual Recognition Arrangement (BIPM)
evidence.finding: The CIPM MRA enables 100+ national metrology institutes to demonstrate equivalence of their measurement standards through key comparisons, confirming reproducibility

scoreReasoning.correspondence: Fundamental constant measurements reproduce across labs and decades; the reproducibility crisis affects soft sciences, not metrology
scoreReasoning.coherence: Reproducibility is a logical consequence of measurement standardization and uncertainty quantification
scoreReasoning.convergence: Broad agreement that reproducibility is the gold standard; debate exists about extent of crisis in specific fields
scoreReasoning.pragmatism: International trade, manufacturing tolerances, and medical diagnostics all depend on reproducible measurement

claim: Radiometric dating methods (carbon-14, potassium-argon, uranium-lead) provide reliable absolute ages for geological and archaeological samples, cross-validated by independent techniques

evidence.title: IntCal20 Northern Hemisphere Radiocarbon Age Calibration Curve (Radiocarbon)
evidence.finding: The IntCal20 calibration curve extends C-14 dating to 55,000 years BP, cross-validated against tree rings (dendrochronology), corals, and speleothems

evidence.title: U-Pb Geochronology (Geochimica)
evidence.finding: Uranium-lead dating of zircon crystals provides the most precise absolute ages for rocks, with uncertainties below 0.1% for billion-year-old samples

scoreReasoning.correspondence: Multiple independent dating methods (C-14, K-Ar, U-Pb, Rb-Sr, luminescence) agree when applied to the same samples; cross-validated against tree-ring chronologies
scoreReasoning.coherence: Based on well-understood nuclear physics — radioactive decay rates are constant and measured to high precision
scoreReasoning.convergence: Broad scientific consensus; young-Earth creationism rejects these methods but offers no competing quantitative chronology
scoreReasoning.pragmatism: Radiometric dating underpins all of geology, paleontology, archaeology, and climate science chronology

claim: Written historical records spanning approximately 5,000 years, cross-referenced with archaeological and scientific dating methods, provide a reliable chronological framework for human civilization

evidence.title: Philosophy of Historiography (SEP)
evidence.finding: Modern historiography uses multiple independent sources, archaeological evidence, and scientific dating to establish chronological frameworks that are robust despite individual source biases

evidence.title: Dendrochronology and Radiocarbon Dating (Antiquity)
evidence.finding: Tree-ring chronologies extending 12,000+ years provide an independent check on historical dates and radiocarbon calibration, confirming key historical timelines

scoreReasoning.correspondence: Cross-referencing written records with archaeology, dendrochronology, and radiometric dating confirms major historical events and timelines
scoreReasoning.coherence: The historical framework is internally consistent when cross-referenced across civilizations (e.g., Egyptian and Mesopotamian chronologies agree at contact points)
scoreReasoning.convergence: Broad scholarly consensus on major chronological frameworks; debates exist on specific dates but not on the overall structure
scoreReasoning.pragmatism: Legal systems, cultural heritage, political boundaries, and education all depend on the historical record

claim: Standardized measurement with quantified uncertainty enables reproducible empirical science across all disciplines

evidence.title: The International System of Units (BIPM)
evidence.finding: The global measurement infrastructure — SI units, GUM uncertainty framework, CIPM MRA — enables consistent science and technology worldwide

evidence.title: Estimating the reproducibility of psychological science (Science)
evidence.finding: Fields with rigorous measurement standards (physics, chemistry, metrology) show high reproducibility; the measurement framework itself is sound even where individual fields struggle

scoreReasoning.correspondence: The measurement framework itself is verified by interlaboratory comparisons achieving part-per-billion agreement
scoreReasoning.coherence: Synthesizes SI standardization, uncertainty quantification, reproducibility, and dating methods into a unified framework for empirical knowledge
scoreReasoning.convergence: Universal agreement that standardized measurement is essential for science; no competing framework exists
scoreReasoning.pragmatism: All of experimental science, engineering, medicine, and international trade depend on standardized, reproducible measurement
